### test_gpu_resident_regions.das

- `test_regions_interleaved_single_steps` - On Qwen2.5-0.5B two sessions in separate mirror regions, prefilled and stepped one row at a time interleaved, each read what that session reads alone, the one-token-off logits the control
- `test_region_taken_after_decode` - Two host-cached sessions sharing one region take it in turn: the loser's device-only rows are saved before the overwrite, and every step of both reads what each session reads alone
- `test_prefill_continues_on_the_device` - A prefill continued from a position past zero - short tail, window-boundary cut, unaligned whole window, second chat turn - runs the window chain over the region's rows within the split bar of one call
- `test_regions_batched_steps` - On Qwen2.5-0.5B a batched step over two sessions in their own regions reads bit for bit what each session reads alone, with no history resync
- `test_regions_batched_steps_split` - With both prompts past the unsplit position, the N-row command's split attention form batches two sessions bit for bit what each session reads alone
- `test_device_home_sessions` - Two device-home sessions with no host cache step singly and batched as a host-cached session alone reads, every call served; a live device-home region is never handed to an outsider, which passes as busy
- `test_device_kv_park_adopt` - A parked device claim hands its rows to one later session, which prefills only the rest within bar of the one-call prefill; the claim refuses an overlong ask, is spent by adoption and dies when its region is taken
- `test_scheduler_device_mode` - A device-mode scheduler emits the host-cached scheduler's tokens on the shared code path, lands picks alone for argmax streams, parks claims within its slots, and a second turn adopts its first turn's rows
- `test_gpu_resident_regions_scheduler_chunks` - A device-home stream prefills a long prompt in device-window chunks rather than the scheduler's 64-token chunks, and a tick hands two streams to one segmented window where the model's window serves
- `test_gpu_resident_regions_guards` - A third device-home session over two occupied regions panics with the reason and counts as busy, while the owners step on reading what they read alone
- `test_gpu_resident_regions_reports` - Every CPU pass reason reads in distinct words, the plan scales K/V bytes with the region count and its weight tally matches the upload within 2%, and a switched-off route reports never attempted
- `test_gpu_resident_regions_passes` - A prefill that skips positions passes to the CPU as gap and one past the region's context as cap, each bringing the session's device rows down to the host first
- `test_scheduler_paged_resident` - A paged scheduler's host-cached streams step on the device token for token as the flat scheduler's, and a second turn attaches the pages its first turn left
- `test_device_pool` - A device-home scheduler's openings outlive their regions in the host pool and later requests take them up token for token as the host prefix cache does; with no pool those requests prefill whole

### test_gpu_serving_declines.das

- `test_resident_unserved_features` - `resident_unserved_features` returns empty for a plain or qwen35-shaped Config and names each unserved attention feature, the sinks and the qkv bias only while their seat is uninstalled
- `test_attn_chain_unserved_features` - The per-op attention chain names interleaved rope and the output bias but serves NEOX, partial rope and the qkv bias, and names each gemma generation's attention by its exact feature list
- `test_dn_plane_format_declines` - On a deltanet shell both the whole-model driver and the per-op chain accept q8, K-quant and per-32 recurrent planes by tag and name an mx4 plane, the per-op chain also naming a layer without the triple
- `test_perop_dense_ffn_mixed_forms` - `perop_dense_ffn_decline` admits a per-32 gate beside a K-quant up and a single-form FFN, and names an mx4 up plane by site and `KqFmt` members in its exact decline text
- `test_resident_cls_decline` - `resident_cls_decline` names a tied classifier over a float token table with no classifier plane, and passes a tied Q8_0 table, a kept q8 copy, a tied K-quant table and an untied classifier
- `test_resident_layer_decline` - `resident_layer_decline` names by layer a recurrent layer without deltanet planes, an untileable out plane, an upward K/V donor, missing planes, off-shape heads and missing expert planes, while serving the shapes the kernels cover
- `test_resident_unserved_moe_features` - For MoE configs `resident_unserved_features` serves softmax routers, router bias, 512 experts at ten picks and gpt-oss's stacks, and names the sigmoid router, selection bias and counts past the select's reach
- `test_kq_fmt_one_row_gemv` - `kq_fmt_one_row_gemv` admits q8 at any width, superblock formats at whole superblocks, per-32 formats at whole 32-blocks and Q4_0 via its repack, and rejects partial blocks and mx4
- `test_dn_metal_plane_formats` - `dn_metal_ok` and `dn_ba_metal_window_ok` admit q8, IQ4_XS, Q2_K, lut IQ3_S, per-32 and mlx recurrent planes by tag, and decline an mx4 beta or out plane and an out width off whole superblocks
- `test_discrete_unstamped_routed_planes` - `discrete_unstamped_plane` passes k4 expert stacks and names, in exact text, an mlx4b routed down plane and an mlx8 shared-expert up plane the discrete homes stamp no kernel for
- `test_moe_metal_expert_formats` - `moe_metal_ok` admits exactly the expert formats with Metal kernels, declining mx4 tags, mlx6b, repacked mx4 and NextN head stacks out of set, and a whole-`KqFmt` walk pins the kernel roster equal to `moe_site_ok`
- `test_moe_metal_expert_count` - The Metal routed block admits 256 and 512 experts and declines 513 on an otherwise unchanged shell, so the select stamps' ladder alone caps the expert count
- `test_moe_metal_expert_weights_scale` - A global `expert_weights_scale` of 2.5 leaves `moe_metal_ok` admitting the routed block, with 513 experts on the same shell declining as the control
- `test_decode_shape_dense_width` - `decode_shape_decline` ignores an off-lattice dense width on a routed model with no dense FFN on both the decode and batch masks, while the same width declines shape on a dense twin and a lattice width passes
- `test_metal_fmt_decline_names_site` - A dense, token-table, classifier or routed plane the Metal kernels cannot read, including nv4 under a per-tensor scale, is named by layer, site and member in the exact decline line, while the gate keeps its enum reason
- `test_metal_graph_decline_names_site` - A sigmoid-gated shared expert or deltanet plane in an unread format, mx4 or nv4 under a per-tensor scale, declines the Metal graph gate and is named by layer, site and member in the exact decline line
- `test_metal_decline_panic_names_site` - On a das_metal build a required-mode plane-format decline panics with the site and member words its warning logs, while a shape decline panics with the bare reason as the control
- `test_mm_tile_widths_64_dense_width` - `mm_tile_widths_64_ok` passes a routed model's off-lattice dense width that no layer dispatches, and declines it once a dense lead layer or a dense twin dispatches it, a lattice width passing
- `test_resident_region_ctx` - `resident_region_ctx` gives each region its integer share of the one binding, keeps a session context under that share or with no cap known, and plans one region for a count under one
- `test_resident_fit_ctx` - `resident_fit_ctx` returns the largest context whose mirror and block-codec shadow fill the room past weights, staged rows, hot pool and fixed rings less its eighth of slack, one position more not fitting
- `test_resident_binding_ctx` - `resident_binding_ctx` is one binding over the widest attention layer's row on hybrid, dense and shared-KV shells alike, block codecs stop at their byte cap where f16 takes the wider range, and no attention reads 0
- `test_resident_mirror_slabs` - `resident_mirror_slabs` cuts owner layers into contiguous least-charge slabs at one stride, seats a sharer at its donor and the NextN head last, pinned by exact slab and base tables, and `resident_mirror_bytes` charges that cut
- `test_slab_limit` - `slab_limit` picks the stride of the fewest slabs that keep every slab under the cap on varied widths, one slab for a cap past the total, one layer's width for a cap under it
- `test_resident_shadow_ctx` - `resident_shadow_ctx` caps a block codec's region context at one binding of the widest K/V row as halves, equal under q8_0 and tq4, halved by a doubled row, 0 for a scalar codec or no attention
- `test_trim_decline_kind` - `resident_trim_decline_is_run_mode` classes route, room, seam, MoE-seat, host-split and a foreign prefill override's declines as the run's and shape or feature declines as the model's, so a lane mints only under the latter
- `test_resident_mirror_codec_ask` - The mirror arms the asked KV codec where the head geometry holds it, steps tq4 down to q8_0 or f16 and f32 to f16 otherwise, the ask restores exactly, and codec names and ordinals round-trip with a named panic
- `test_plan_room` - `plan_room` gives the tier cap less WDDM's 27 percent or the 2 GiB floor with no OS answer, the OS budget less other processes and a 1 GiB reserve when it answers, and a pinned cap whole
- `test_heap_room` - With dasVulkan, `heap_room` takes the largest device-local heap by live budget on a discrete card and sums every heap on an integrated one, and `uma_spill_pick` picks only a coherent host-heap type
- `test_resident_hot_slots` - `resident_hot_slots` and `resident_hot_fit` size the hot expert pool to the slots beside the mirror up to 32 taken from its context, an ask from the floor's room, none under four, charging the chain scratch only with a pool
- `test_resident_arm_floor` - The capped mirror's arm floor follows built-in, env and pin with a 256 minimum and a strict pin raising it, the fewest leading MoE layers go to the host, and a strict context past a region's binding declines
- `test_routed_slots_fit` - With dasVulkan, `rd_routed_slots_fit` admits a rows-times-picks product up to the 128 routed slots (16x8, 12x10, 4x32) and rejects one past it (16x9, 5x32)
- `test_mtp_seat_owner` - Under a probe decode override the speculative seats are read only when its owner claims the model, returning the seat's rows cap and cold reason, while both round entries always open the common round
- `test_land_pick` - A landed pick is returned once by the next `sample_` over the logits argmax, a second landing before it panics and keeps the first, and the CPU round refuses a session with an unsampled pick
- `test_mtp_round_panics` - The speculative round fails closed on fake seats: a pick ask beside a sampled walk panics before any draft, and a rollback seat declining after a served verify panics naming the override
- `test_mtp_verify_snapshot` - On fake seats a recurrent round without a rollback seat takes the CPU snapshot sized to the state, a plain one takes none, and a serving rollback seat rolls a reject back and re-seeds the carry from row 0
- `test_peel_shape_arms` - `rdec_peel_shape_why` fits dense, NextN and per-layer-embedding shells, names a hyper-connection chain and a recurrent model without the in-order rows command, and no unarmed model takes the segmented window
- `test_resident_ring_mirror` - On a gemma-4-26B shell at 32768 x 4 the sliding rings hold 1536 rows a layer, the ringed mirror is under a seventh of the flat one, and the house flat plan re-costed with rings fits the 32 GB card's room
- `test_trim_lane_ring_pin` - The KV ring pin leaves a trimmed vulkan lane's image identity unchanged while moving its planned mirror, and mapping a trimmed lane declines naming the ring pin, a planar shell mapping cleanly as control
- `test_kv_ring_floor_check` - `kv_ring_floor_check` continues a call at or past the session's ring floor, panics on one under it, and a start at 0 clears the floor so the same call then continues
- `test_resident_host_layers_pin` - The host-layers pin reads back, lifts on a negative and restores as found, and `resident_host_layers_want` passes an ask capped at the routed count only where the plain split form takes the model
- `test_ple_proj_dim_gates` - `metal_ple_dev_ok` serves any dim and ple width and names a PLE table off its format's blocks by offset and block, `gk_bf16_pairs` needs an even dim and base, and Vulkan names an f16 panel past the storage range
- `test_ple_f32_tile_gates` - On a Vulkan shell the f32 PLE rows take the staged tile only with the knob on, dims on the 32 k step and subgroup 32, `pf_f32_split` never splits past the scratch, and odd dims take the bf16 halfword stamp
- `test_h128_twin_gate` - On a Vulkan device shell `h128_twin_on` holds only for a coopmat device at subgroup 32, declining a wave64 device and one without coopmat
- `test_vk_subgroup_pin` - On the live Vulkan device the tier pins DASLLAMA_VK_SUBGROUP only where it differs from the device width and is pinnable, and the KHR kq tile and coopmat mode resolve at the pinned width
- `test_pf_chunk_cap` - `pf_chunk_cap` holds the prefill ramp at `PF_CHUNK_MAX` layers a submit on a discrete device shell and caps it at one layer on an integrated one
- `test_expert_heat_profile` - An expert heat profile written for a layers-by-experts shape reads back element for element, while another shape, a missing file, a bad magic or a short file reads empty
- `test_kv_codec_serving_rule` - `kv_codec_served` serves tq4 as asked on a plain 32-wide head, steps it to q8_0 naming a qkv bias or a non-power-of-two head, and lands tq4 and q8_0 at f16 on a 48-wide head
- `test_baked_host_layers` - `vk_baked_host_layers` reads a lane's host-layer split as the `host_split` marker entry's woff, and answers -1 for a plan minted before the marker or an empty plan
- `test_vulkan_tower_route_before_a_device` - With no Vulkan device up, `vulkan_tower_front_route` answers false without a null dereference, so the scratch sizing can ask it ahead of the arm

### test_gpu_tier.das

- `test_gpu_tier_contract` - After resetting the home seats, uninstalled rdec slots decline, installed doubles receive exactly the forwarded arguments, the want state round-trips with one rail arming the tier, and the arm hook resets to unarmed
- `test_gpu_tier_resident_ask` - `gpu_resident_requested` turns on for an explicit resident want or the measured-best set and otherwise follows the ambient DASLLAMA_GPU, and resident alone does not turn `gpu_want_auto` on
- `test_gpu_cpu_passes` - `gpu_cpu_passes_` lists one row per CPU-pass reason that fired, in reason order with its words and exact count, and re-setting the reasons starts the counts from zero
- `test_rdec_readback_reaches_the_doubles` - The KV read and sync forwarders hand the installed doubles their layer and row window, and the read double's writes land through the caller's K and V pointers
- `test_rdec_carry_seat` - The speculative carry seat is uninstalled until its own install, then forwards the row to the double, which writes through the destination the forwarder handed it
- `test_rdec_draft_seat` - The NextN draft seat declines unset, forwards token, row, hydrate start and pick ask to its double, survives an unset and reinstall, and the head's norms block sits past the trunk's q/k slots
- `test_rdec_verify_seat` - The same-slab verify seat declines and steps no rows unset, and installed forwards ids, position, row count and pick ask, landing picks and hidden rows always and logits only without the pick ask
- `test_rdec_rollback_seat` - The verify's rollback seat declines without reaching any double while unset, and once installed forwards the committed row and returns the double's answer
- `test_rdec_head_warm_seat` - The head warm seat keeps no ask and answers 0 rows unset, forwards the ask and row count installed, and the head's K/V sync and read forward layer n_layers with its row window
- `test_rdec_dn_seats` - The hybrid deltanet seats install apart and forward the layer, beta/alpha offset, uploaded row count, owned state pointer and prefill slot handoff to their doubles
- `test_rdec_prefill_ids_seam` - The ids-form prefill seat declines embed setup and f32 upload unset, the f32 table charge is zero past its cap, and installed doubles receive block, format, scale, vocab and positions
- `test_dlim_vulkan_tag_dn_native` - `dlim_vulkan_tag` changes when `dn_native` is set, so the vulkan image identity distinguishes a lane with native deltanet planes
- `test_kernel_dump_save` - `kernel_dump_save` writes text and word payloads byte-exact under the knob's directory, succeeds writing nothing with the knob unset, and answers false for a missing directory
- `test_segments_served_by_override` - Under a probe override with no mrope or deepstack arm, two plain sessions take the segments form, a per-row rope or deepstack session declines it until cleared, and no active override means no form
- `test_gpu_said_once` - `gpu_said_once` says and records a reason once, answers false and records nothing on a repeat, adds a new reason, and says a reason again after the set is cleared
- `test_unset_seats_name_their_module` - Calling the unset N-row token command or per-layer PLE planes seat panics with text naming `require dasllama/dasllama_math_vulkan`, the module that installs them
- `test_override_announces` - In child runs, each GPU override announces its exact line, naming setter and env spelling, only where it moves off its default, and on Metal the fuse knob announces once a state, at context init under =0
- `test_home_words` - In child runs a declined model falls to the per-op rails, or to the CPU rails under DASLLAMA_CUDA=1 on a dasCUDA build, and each home's dry-bake arm refuses the other home's config by name
- `test_pf_window_rows_rounding` - `pf_window_rows` rounds a pin or the knob down to a 128-row multiple with a 128 floor, and with neither set serves the driver's pick, the narrow default before one, a pin outranking it
- `test_ple_window_seed` - `ple_window_seed` fills a four-slot window with the ids before position n oldest first, -1 in slots before the prompt start, keeping the window's length
- `test_vulkan_trim_default` - The vulkan lane's trim knob defaults to trimmed, and with no `set_vulkan_trim` lever set `vulkan_trim` follows the knob
- `test_gpu_tier_seats_put_back` - The home's entry installers run again over the test doubles so later files see the home's seats, and the tier stays unarmed afterward

### test_groupn.das

- `test_q8q8_groupn` - Under every kernel backend the q8 region-list GEMV matches three per-region single GEMVs within 1e-6 relative and an fp64 dequant dot within its per-block bar, a 0.05 poison past the bar the control
- `test_groupn_bias_fold` - Under every kernel backend the biased q8 and mx4 region-list GEMVs equal the unbiased GEMV plus the per-region bias added after, bit for bit
- `test_mx4q8_groupn` - Under every kernel backend, repacked where it needs it, the mx4 region-list GEMV matches three per-region single mx4 GEMVs within 1e-6 relative

### test_interpreter.das

- `test_utterance_window` - The interpreter's utterance window pads the speech a quarter second each side clamped to the take, never exceeds the cap, and a take idles out only with no speech open
- `test_listen_drain` - The listen drain appends frames under the gain clamped to plus or minus 1 with the appended frames' rms, clips the padded window, and its speech marks decide the cut at end, at cap, idle or none
- `test_turn_ledger` - The turn ledger counts only in-flight turns and finds a turn by number, and landing text moves a turn transcribing to translating to speaking, or to empty when the text has no words
- `test_smoke_hears_translates_and_speaks` - The interpreter example's smoke run hears a Russian clip, translates it to English carrying its words, speaks it and ends on the turn; a non-audio clip and a missing ASR model are refused by name

### test_jobque_tripwire.das

- `test_bare_queue_panics` - In a child process the engine's first dispatch on an unconfigured job queue exits non-zero, naming setup_dasllama_jobque, and the program never runs on
- `test_allow_bare_jobque_warns_and_runs` - With DASLLAMA_ALLOW_BARE_JOBQUE=1 a child's dispatch on an unconfigured queue still warns that it is not configured but exits 0 and runs to its end
- `test_team_job_panic_exits_nonzero` - A panic inside a team chunk on a two-thread queue ends the child process non-zero, the report naming the job exception and the panic, and the program never runs on
- `test_configured_queue_is_silent` - On a configured engine job queue maybe_parallel_for dispatches through the counted parallel arm without tripping the bare-queue check

### test_kernel_backend.das

- `test_portable_backend_always_registered` - The kernel-backend registry self-populates at init: portable is registered, a non-empty registered backend is auto-activated, and an unknown name is not registered
- `test_select_and_pin` - Select and pin by name activate portable, an unknown name in either is a no-op keeping the current backend, and the for-load pick activates a registered backend
- `test_seat_restores_the_pin` - `restore_kernel_backend` puts back exactly the seat it was given: an unpinned seat clears a later pin and reactivates its backend, a pinned seat restores pin and backend over a for-load reselect
- `test_with_kernel_backend` - `with_kernel_backend` runs its block on the pinned backend and puts the seat back, refuses an unknown backend without running the block, and an earlier pin survives a nested pin on a second backend
- `test_kq_registries` - Where dasLLVM mounts, every kq format carries all eight tune registries or none with the reference row first, every format but q8 has rm rows with a witness keyed alike per perm, and no format's kernel row is another's
- `test_backend_availability_predicate` - A priority-99 backend whose availability predicate answers false is skipped by the for-load select and refused by pin, and the probe reads unregistered names unavailable and portable available
- `test_batch_backend_pin` - The batch backend follows the active one unpinned, an unknown or repack donor on a row-major active backend is rejected, a row-major donor's pin survives reselection, and clearing restores whole-backend slots
- `test_batch_only_backends_refuse_the_whole_seat` - Every batch-only backend, including each metal, vulkan or cuda donor the build registers, leaves the active backend and pin unchanged under pin or select, and on macOS vulkan is unavailable without DASLLAMA_VK_MAC
- `test_env_pin_refuses_what_cannot_take` - A pin that cannot take, unregistered or batch-only, is refused by name and panics only when DASLLAMA_PIN_BACKEND named it, warning when pinned in process, and sets no pin
- `test_accel_float_batch` - The Accelerate float-batch override (fp32, bf16, BNNS f16 lane, strips) matches the portable batch matmul within a relative bar that reds a poisoned element, and below the min-ntok gate falls through bit-exact

### test_kernel_coverage.das

- `test_metal_kernel_coverage` - Census over the small-model zoo on a Metal device: at least 40 distinct kernels dispatched on an unfiltered run, and each declared blind-spot entry names a compiled kernel that no stocked carrier dispatches
- `test_vulkan_kernel_coverage_serving` - The Vulkan serving census over the local zoo, codec carriers, coopmat mode sweep and tower rows dispatches at least 24 distinct kernels, and every declared blind spot names a seeded kernel with zero dispatches
- `test_vulkan_kernel_coverage_rail` - Device-free: the compile-time Vulkan lens spec seeds the coverage census with at least 40 kernels, every one reading zero after a reset

### test_kqformat.das

- `test_kqfmt_under_dat_key_radix` - With dasVulkan, every `KqFmt` member's int id sits strictly under `DAT_KEY_FMTS`, so the decode block's layer key never hands one layer another layer's mirror
- `test_kqfmt_enum_values` - Every `KqFmt` member's int value is pinned to a literal 0 through 25, the ids device tags and stream codes key off
- `test_kqfmt_affine_rows` - The mlx affine members are per-32, unstamped on the discrete homes and id-less, with literal quant bytes, 2-byte scale unit, ggml types and disk bytes, and `mlx_affine_ggml_type` maps only real bit and group pairs
- `test_kqfmt_predicates` - `kq_sb` holds exactly for the superblock lattice on both enum and int ids, and the per-32, nv4 and iq3s4 members' strides, ggml types, schema ids and the Q4_0 codebook match literals
- `test_kqfmt_strides` - Every K-quant format's quant and scale strides and their named constants equal the literal byte layouts, the IQ4_NL codebook is upstream's monotonic table, and the iq3s4 codebook steps odd magnitudes by 2
- `test_kqfmt_grid` - `IQ3S_GRID` matches upstream's iq3s_grid at its first and last entries, and the worker-safe `iq3s_grid` local agrees with it at sampled entries
- `test_kqfmt_id_bridge` - `kq_schema_id` maps each lattice format to its pinned kernel id, and the int-id stride forms answer the same strides as the enum forms for every one
- `test_kqfmt_elems_and_stream` - Every descriptor row's disk bytes equal ggml's block bytes and its schema id round-trips or is -1 off the lattice, bytes per weight follow the stride table, and every stream code is pinned
- `test_iq3xxs_tables` - The halved IQ3_XXS grid matches its local with every byte even in 2..30 or 31, ksigns carry even parity in bit 7, and `f16_half_bits` halves normal, negative and edge-subnormal f16 exactly
- `test_b32_plane_words` - Each per-32 format's quant words and scale bytes sum to its descriptor's disk bytes, and every per-32 and mlx block fits the one-block scratch
- `test_kq_fmt_row_demotion` - `kq_fmt_row_ok` and `kq_fmt_expert_ok` move Q4_0 and IQ4_NL rows off the superblock lattice to their per-32 planes, other formats off it to q8, keep q51 and q5032 on 32-multiples, and send rows off 32 to q8
- `test_kq_fmt_stamp` - `kq_fmt_stamp` binds each `KqFmt` member to its own tag type, so a per-format overload family resolves k4 and q51 to their overloads and every other member to its named tag
- `test_gguf_need_tensor_refuses` - `gguf_need_tensor` on a tensor absent from the file panics with text naming both the family and the tensor
- `test_gguf_decline_unread_types` - A tensor of an unread ggml type declines the load naming the tensor, its type and the served type to requantize to, Q8_0 for a type with no row, while a file of served types loads
- `test_metal_b32_block_constants` - The literal block constants of the Metal per-32 GEMV, tile and embed classes (BE, QW, SH, B32W, B32S, B32E) equal the per-32 descriptor rows' elements, quant bytes and scale bytes
- `test_metal_kq_table_constants` - The Metal K-quant token-table gathers' literal SB_UINTS and QH0 equal the k4, k5 and codebook formats' superblock quant words and k5's qh strip start
- `test_load_report_row_names_site` - `gguf_tensor_role` reads the role off a tensor name, `kq_site_words` turns it into site words, and `conv_row_name` renders exact rows naming site, disk type and served plane or conversion
- `test_kq_tile_stamped` - `kq_tile_stamped` drops a member word's every tail, a pair word's one tail and with `!b32` every non-per-32 member, keeping the superblock member once `!b32` is gone

### test_kquant.das

The K-quant and grid formats: plane dequants, dots, the grp repack, the bf16 panel, tiles and GEMVs against in-test references, and the model-gated load cells. Skips: an interpreted run and a missing stocked model (the model cells), no gen backend registered (batch groupn), a backend with no kq slots (the repacked-plane serve cell), a format whose stamp is a bf16 tile (the 4-token tile cells), and a build without dasLLVM (the affine members' row-major cells).

- `test_q4k_synthetic` - The Q4_K, Q5_K and Q6_K superblock dequants reproduce hand-packed superblocks, written in the pack direction, bit for bit against the element formula
- `test_kq_transcode_planes` - Every K-quant, grid, iq2 lattice and per-32 format's transcoded plane pair dequants a hand-packed synthetic block bit for bit to the file dequant or the format's element formula
- `test_mlx_affine_kernels` - The five MLX affine members dequant hand-packed blocks to scale x q + bias exactly (another packing order misses), and their dot, groupn, grp, batch, dense-router and row-major kernels match the scalar row dots
- `test_q51_kernels` - Under the portable backend at a 704-wide row, the q51 scalar dot matches an fp64 plane-dequant reference and its GPU gather, groupn, grp repack, batch and dense routers bit-match the disk-order scalar dots
- `test_iq4nl32_kernels` - Under the portable backend at a 2560-wide row, the iq4nl32 scalar dot matches an fp64 plane-dequant reference and its GPU gather, groupn, grp repack, batch and dense routers bit-match the disk-order scalar dots
- `test_q4032_kernels` - Under the portable backend at a 1408-wide row, the q4032 scalar dot matches an fp64 plane-dequant reference and its GPU gather, groupn, grp repack, batch and dense routers bit-match the disk-order scalar dots
- `test_q5032_kernels` - Under the portable backend at a 1408-wide row, the q5032 scalar dot matches an fp64 plane-dequant reference and its GPU gather, groupn, grp repack, batch and dense routers bit-match the disk-order scalar dots
- `test_kq_dots` - For every superblock format at n = 512, 1024 and 3072, the integer-domain `dot_kq` over LCG-distinct superblocks lands within 1e-4 relative of an fp64 dot over the plane dequant and Q8_K activation
- `test_kq_gemv_rows` - For every superblock format, the portable `matmul_kq` over eight LCG-distinct rows bit-matches the per-row disk dots, pinning the per-row quant and scale plane strides past row 0
- `test_kq_gemm_disk_batch` - For every superblock format, the disk-order three-token batch GEMM bit-matches the GEMV run a token at a time and lands within 1e-4 of the largest output of an fp64 plane-dequant reference
- `test_kq_repack_grp` - For every superblock format, the grp repack at mr 4, 8 and 16 keeps row dots and row dequants bit-exact to the disk plane, and at mr 16 the bf16 panels hold each weight within a bf16 step at its pair slot
- `test_kq_tile` - For every superblock format not stamped as a bf16 tile, the 4-token kq tile over grp-repacked planes, with a 3-token GEMV tail, is bit-exact to one full GEMV per token
- `test_kq_declined_family_keeps_the_reference_layout` - A superblock format with no emitter arm reads a false witness and keeps the reference layout companion mr = 4, whatever perm the profile names
- `test_kq_groupn` - The region-list kq GEMV bit-matches per-row disk dots on disk planes and per-region rows-core calls on grp slices, under shared and per-region activations, up to the 122B expert slice shapes
- `test_kq_batch_groupn` - On the gen backend, the fused-prefill `matmul_kq_batch_groupn` over runs of 1, 4, 6 and 13 tokens per region bit-matches per-(region, token) rows-core calls, up to the 122B slice shapes
- `test_quantize_bs` - The bs Q8 quantizer writes the same quants and scales as `quantize_q8_0` byte for byte, plus per-16 sums equal to the exact integer sums of those quants
- `test_kq_load_layout` - A portable-pinned kq-native load of Qwen3-4B Q4_K_M, Qwen3.5 NVFP4 and gemma-4-26B Q4_0 places each tagged tensor at its cursor offset: plane dequant prefixes match the file dequant, and `mm_b_kq` matches the per-position GEMV
- `test_kq_q40_repacked_planes` - On the box's own backend, gemma-4-26B Q4_0's repacked expert gate and up regions dot the fused tensor's rows exactly on an exact Q8_K row, the tied k6 embedding matches the file, and the region-list dispatch matches per-region GEMVs
- `test_kq_fused_qkv_slices` - Phi-3.5 Q4_K_M's fused attn_qkv splits into k5 q and k slices whose plane dequants match the file dequant within 1e-3 relative L2, the k slice at its dim x qd source offset
- `test_kq_phi3_longrope_factors` - Loaded Phi-3.5 Q4_K_M, whose context runs past the original 4096, carries the file's 48 `rope_factors_long` values bit for bit as `rope_freqs`, and they differ from the short set
- `test_kq_ple_table` - gemma-4-E2B Q4_K_M's per-layer token table loads on the k5 plane, not a silent q8 fallback, and its first 16 rows dequant within 1e-3 relative L2 of the file dequant
- `test_per32_tables_cpu` - On four per-32 local mints, every table site loads native, `embed_row` rows match the file dequant bit for bit (job lanes too), and classifier and eh_proj rows match the file rows' dot within f32 reassociation
- `test_iq3xxs_planes` - The iq3xxs plane pair dequants a hand-packed superblock bit for bit to an independent recomputation off the disk bytes through the grid and ksigns tables
- `test_iq4nl_planes` - The iq4nl plane dequant matches a codebook recomputation exactly and reads the same values on a jobque team lane as on the main thread, and q8 plane transcode and grp repack both panic
- `test_kq_plane_sb_metal_blob_form` - For the iq2, iq3 and iq4xs formats, `dequant_kq_plane_sb` over the Metal-blob split scale plane reads random-byte superblocks to exactly the row form's values
- `test_vbmi_lattice_tables` - The VBMI lattice tables are self-consistent on any box: every iq2 and iq3 grid byte round-trips through its packed code and alphabet, and `pm1_of` matches the scalar +-1 expansion of all 256 ksigns bytes
- `test_kq_gpu_gather_iq` - For the iq4xs, iq3 and iq2xxs codebook formats, the GPU expert gather's two-word device scale rows decode back to the plane's f16 d and sub-scales, and grp-plane gathers equal disk-order gathers byte for byte
- `test_kq_gpu_gather_grp` - For the k3, k6 and nv4 planes, the GPU expert gather off grp-repacked planes writes byte-identical quant and scale device bytes to the gather off disk-order planes
- `test_kq_gpu_gather_nv4_row` - The nv4 GPU gather writes each 20-byte device scale row as the sixteen UE4M3 codes verbatim, then its slice's site-scale f32 word, per expert and off disk or grp planes alike
- `test_nv4_rm_gemv_ue4m3_codes` - The live nv4 row-major GEMV decodes each of the 128 UE4M3 scale codes, subnormals and the NaN code included, to `ue4m3_half_f32`'s exact float word on a constant-nibble, all-127 row
- `test_q8_plane_row_f32` - `q8_plane_row_f32` reads Q8_0 rows repacked at grp4 biased and grp16 unbiased, with and without a row tail, back as q x the block's f32 scale bit for bit, where an f16-rounded scale misses

### test_kv_codec.das

- `test_kv_layout` - On synthetic Configs (uniform, gemma4-style ragged SWA, E-series shared KV), the f32 session's per-layer byte prefixes match an independent walk, shared layers alias their source slab, and the caches size exactly
- `test_kv_layout_f16` - An f16 session's KV byte prefixes are twice the element prefixes and its caches half the f32 bytes, and a mixed f16 K / f32 V session walks each side at its own width
- `test_kv_layout_q8` - A q8_0 session's KV byte prefixes and cache sizes are 34 bytes per 32 elements exactly, and a mixed q8_0 K / f16 V session walks each side at its own width
- `test_kv_store_row_q8` - q8_0 `kv_store_row` reads back within half a step plus f16-scale rounding, re-quantizing its own dequant is byte-identical, and a head-slot partial store lands at its block offset
- `test_kv_runs_flat` - On a flat session, `kv_runs` returns exactly one identity run (row0 equal to j0) for whole, offset and one-row windows, none for empty or inverted ones, and `kv_phys_row` is the identity
- `test_kv_store_row_f16` - f16 `kv_store_row` stores every element as the round-to-nearest-even half of the source clamped to +-65504, so out-of-range values read back finite at the clamp
- `test_kv_codec_signs` - `tq4_fill_signs` fills only +1 and -1, and the 32-wide sign vector is a prefix of the 64-wide one
- `test_kv_codec_fwht` - The signed FWHT rotation preserves a dot of two 64-wide rows within 1e-4 relative, and `fwht_unsign_row` inverts it to within 1e-5 per element
- `test_kv_codec_tq4_roundtrip` - tq4 quantize then dequant lands every element within one quantization step (q4_0 saturates the positive extreme), and re-quantizing the dequant is byte-identical
- `test_kv_codec_q8_dots` - Over a q8_0 KV row, `dot_q8kv` matches the float block reference within 1e-3 relative, and the integer-accumulating `dot_q8q8kv` matches its block reference bit for bit
- `test_kv_codec_q8_axpy` - `axpy_q8kv` adds a scaled q8_0 KV row into the destination bit for bit as one mad per element with the block scale, on any tuned perm
- `test_kv_codec_tq4_dot` - `dot_q8tq4kv` of a hand-built Q8 query with a tq4 KV row matches the integer nibble block reference bit for bit
- `test_kv_codec_tq4_axpy` - `axpy_tq4kv` adds a scaled tq4 KV row into the destination bit for bit as one mad per nibble element with the block scale, on any tuned perm
- `test_kv_codec_f16` - The f16 row convert round-trips per element as scalar RNE with the +-65504 clamp, `dot_f16` matches the scalar mad chain within 1e-3 relative, and `axpy_f16` is bit-exact per element
- `test_kv_f16_decode` - On stories15M, a 24-step greedy decode over an f16 KV cache emits the f32 cache's token ids with final logits within 1.0, and fused and standard decode under f16 agree bit for bit
- `test_kv_f16_prefill_vs_decode` - On stories15M with an f16 KV cache, a 16-token classic prefill leaves the logits and both cache planes bit-identical to decoding the same tokens one at a time
- `test_kv_q8_decode` - On SmolLM2-135M under the portable backend, teacher-forced logits over q8_0 and q8_0-K/f16-V caches stay within 4.0 of the f16 cache's, and fused and standard decode under q8_0 agree bit for bit
- `test_kv_q8_prefill_vs_decode` - On SmolLM2-135M with a q8_0 KV cache, a 16-token classic prefill leaves the logits and both cache planes bit-identical to decoding the same tokens one at a time
- `test_kv_store_row_roundtrip` - f32 `kv_store_row` lands a whole row and a head-slot partial row at their layer, row and sub-offset addresses, reading back exactly
- `test_kv_capacity_tripwire` - A capacity tripwire: on stories15M cut to seq_len 8, a 16-token prefill and a decode step at position 8 both panic before any store, while an 8-token eval at capacity runs
- `test_kv_codec_side_stamp` - The `kv_codec_side` macro binds each of the four codecs to its own cache-pointer type at the same address, and nested once per side yields all sixteen K x V type pairs
- `test_kv_codec_step_down` - A tq4 KV ask on Qwen2.5-0.5B, whose attention carries a Q/K/V bias, serves at q8_0 in a session, a pool and a chat, q8_0 asked stays q8_0, and bias-free Qwen3-0.6B keeps tq4

### test_kv_paged.das

- `test_kv_pool_layout` - A paged KV pool on the E-series shared-KV Config maps shared layers to their source's blob, sizes each blob's K and V row bytes by its own dtype, and allocates nothing up front
- `test_kv_pool_alloc_release` - Pool groups allocate LIFO from a free list that grows geometrically (4 then 8 then 16), release returns a group at refcount 0, and growth inside a reserve moves no blob and keeps written rows
- `test_kv_ensure_growth` - `kv_ensure` grows a paged session's block table to ceil(upto / page) pages, idempotently and never shrinking, and releasing returns every page so the pool's free list is back to capacity
- `test_kv_runs_paged` - Paged `kv_runs` maps windows through the block table: physically consecutive pages merge into one run, shuffled pages split at every straddled boundary, and `kv_phys_row` follows the same table
- `test_kv_paged_memory_proportional` - A paged pool's cache bytes at 10 positions are under half the flat slabs sized for seq_len 1024, and grow only as the context deepens to 600 positions
- `test_kv_paged_store_roundtrip` - A `kv_store_row` through the paged layer base and `kv_phys_row` reads back exactly at the block-table row, and shared-KV layers' K and V bases alias their source layer's
- `test_kv_paged_decode` - On stories15M, two paged f32 sessions interleaved on one pool fragment its pages yet match their flat references bit for bit in logits over 40 decode steps and in every cache row
- `test_kv_paged_q8` - On SmolLM2-135M, two paged q8_0 sessions interleaved on one pool fragment its pages yet match flat q8_0 references bit for bit in logits over 40 decode steps and in every cache row
- `test_kv_paged_prefill` - On stories15M, a 21-token prefill straddling three 8-row pages matches flat prefill bit for bit in logits and cache rows, and eight greedy decode steps on top stay bit-exact
- `test_kv_paged_eval_batch` - On stories15M, `eval_batch` over three paged sessions of ragged depth on one pool, one crossing a page mid-decode, matches flat sessions' logits bit for bit for six steps and the deepest cache rows byte for byte

### test_kv_prefix.das

- `test_prefix_accounting` - Prefix-cache refcounts on a synthetic Config: inserted pages outlive the donor, an attach shares whole pages and copies the partial one up to one token short, a divergent prompt takes nothing, and release returns every page
- `test_prefix_lru_budget` - A prefix cache capped at two pages LRU-drops the oldest of three donated pages while the session still holding it keeps it alive, and a chain whose first page dropped attaches nothing
- `test_prefix_tail_edges` - Past the whole hits, a page sharing no row is not copied, each donation's next page is a candidate the prompt picks by shared rows, a partial take is an LRU touch, and a link to a dropped page attaches nothing
- `test_prefix_first_page_edges` - With no whole-page hit, the first page sharing the most leading rows is copied and its chain credited, the same prompt again stops a token short, a prompt sharing no first row takes nothing, and an evicted first page leaves the candidates
- `test_prefix_ring_floor` - Each cached page carries its donor's ring floor: an attach and its probe cut to the longest run ending at or past every taken page's floor, and the session, or a sharing carrier, is left at the deepest floor taken
- `test_prefix_verify_tokens` - Hashes only route: a cache entry whose stored tokens no longer match the prompt, as in a hash collision, refuses to attach, and the probe reads 0 too
- `test_prefix_checkpoint_accounting` - A recurrent session's donation is one checkpoint: whole pages shared, the last row's page copied even on a boundary, the donor's state restored on attach, a prompt it covers whole or leaves early attaching nothing
- `test_prefix_checkpoint_budget` - With `max_states` 2, a third checkpoint drops the one used longest ago, not the oldest inserted, returning its pages, and a budget of zero keeps no checkpoint
- `test_prefix_checkpoint_kinds_and_bytes` - The checkpoint byte budget sums each checkpoint's bytes and evicts tails before openings, a tail a prefill stops at is promoted to an opening, and the checkpoint just inserted is never the victim
- `test_prefix_checkpoint_newest_stands` - The checkpoint just inserted is never evicted: with only openings to drop, the opening used longest ago goes, and under a byte budget smaller than one checkpoint the newest stands alone
- `test_prefix_checkpoint_shared_pages` - Two checkpoints of one conversation sharing a page are charged to the byte budget as the sum of their own figures minus that page's bytes, and release returns the budget to zero
- `test_prefix_checkpoint_at` - `prefix_checkpoint_at_` stops a recurrent prefill at the caller's opening, else one an earlier checkpoint shares, a token short of a prompt held whole, and nowhere under a page past the hit or without recurrent state
- `test_prefix_pool_carrier` - A device carrier session shares the whole pages the cache holds and writes the rest, a snapshot taken elsewhere files as opening or tail, and the split attach shares every page of the deepest opening and restores state
- `test_prefix_spare_snapshots` - Snapshots of dropped checkpoints wait for reuse with their arrays, at most two outside the byte budget, an empty cache hands out an empty snapshot, and release drops the spares
- `test_prefix_insert_reasons` - `prefix_insert_` answers an empty string for a kept, touched or dense donation, and a refusal naming its cause: a token list short of the session's position, no evaled row, or a cache keeping no checkpoints
- `test_prefix_snapshot_stop_touched` - A snapshot filed at a stop the cache already keeps adds no checkpoint, insert count, byte charge or page reference, but marks the kept one used now and promotes it to an opening
- `test_prefix_checkpoint_side_state` - A checkpoint keeps the n-gram side input's last tokens and conv history as taken, restoring them on attach, and a snapshot of another state size is refused and leaves the session unchanged
- `test_prefix_warm_equals_cold` - On stories15M under classic prefill, shared prefix pages plus a tail eval reproduce the cold prefill's logits and eight greedy decode steps bit for bit, and a divergent suffix matches its own cold run
- `test_prefix_tail_copy` - On stories15M, a prompt sharing rows of the page past the whole hits takes a copy, the donor's page staying the cache's alone, and lands the cold prefill's logits bit for bit for four row splits

### test_math_activations.das

The activation, norm and fp32 GEMM kernels - softmax_sink, swiglu_oai(4), softcap(4), sigmoid_gate(4), silu_mul4, silu4_batch, l2_norm_rows and gemm_f32 / _jo / _uk_4x16 - against closed forms and in-test fp64 references over shapes that reach every tail; and the scalar kernels - rmsnorm, silu / gelu, the swiglu / geglu gates, softmax, parallel_argmax and hlse - against hand-computed values.

- `test_softmax_sink` - Over lengths 1 to 1025, `softmax_sink` matches an fp64 reference with negligible and dominant sinks, the row plus sink mass sums to one, and shifting scores and sink together leaves the row unchanged
- `test_softcap` - `softcap` and `softcap4` equal cap x tanh(x / cap) within a cap-scaled bar at caps 30 and 50 over lengths 1 to 1025, move every element, and never leave the band
- `test_sigmoid_gate` - `sigmoid_gate` and `sigmoid_gate4` scale each element by the logistic of its gate, matching an fp64 reference over lengths 1 to 1025 including every vector tail
- `test_swiglu_oai` - `swiglu_oai` and `swiglu_oai4` match an fp64 reference carrying the gate limit 7 and up band +-7, and a gate or up value past the limit reads exactly as the limit while gates inside it stay distinct
- `test_silu_mul4` - `silu_mul4` overwrites every element of a sentinel destination with a x silu(z), matching an fp64 reference over lengths 1 to 1025
- `test_silu4_batch` - `silu4_batch` lands the same bits as `silu4` over the whole buffer, splitting rows across lanes only with a job queue, and runs whole where an odd row length or a single row forbids the split
- `test_l2_norm_rows` - `l2_norm_rows` matches an fp64 reference and drives every row to unit length across row shapes, and an all-zero or tiny row divides by the eps floor instead
- `test_gemm_f32` - `gemm_f32` matches an fp64 C + A x B within a K-scaled bar on every declared shape, a 0.01 poison leg falls outside that bar, and `gemm_f32_jo` is bit-identical to it
- `test_zero_size` - A zero element or row count leaves the buffer untouched in every activation and norm kernel: softmax_sink, softcap, silu, sigmoid gate, swiglu_oai, silu_mul4 and l2_norm_rows
- `test_rmsnorm` - `rmsnorm` maps a constant vector to ones, gives unit mean square under unit weights, and passes the weight through for an rms-1 input, each within a small tolerance
- `test_silu` - `silu` matches hand-computed values to 1e-4 including the negative dip, saturates to x and 0 at plus and minus 20, and `silu` / `gelu` with size zero leave the array untouched without an index fault
- `test_gate` - Scalar `swiglu` / `geglu` equal the activation-then-multiply reference bit for bit on 12 mixed-sign inputs, and the exp4 fused `swiglu4` / `geglu4` stay within 1e-3 max abs diff of them
- `test_softmax` - `softmax` yields an order-preserving distribution summing to 1, uniform output on equal scores, equal results for inputs shifted by 1000 (max-subtraction), and a no-op on size zero
- `test_argmax_hlse` - `parallel_argmax` returns the first maximum on empty, single, ordinary and tied rows, and `hlse` matches the scalar exp(x - mx) sum to 1e-6 across a 4-wide group plus tail, zero on empty

### test_math_elementwise.das

The [tuned] elementwise kernels - dot, dot_bf16, axpy, add_inplace, add_scale_inplace, mul_inplace, scale_inplace, copy_floats - swept over tail lengths against fp64 references.

- `test_dot` - Over tail lengths 1 to 1025, `dot` bit-matches an fp64 sum on dyadic inputs fp32 cannot round, and on unit-range inputs lands within an n-squared bar a 0.5 poison leg falls outside
- `test_dot_bf16` - Over tail lengths 1 to 1025, `dot_bf16` bit-matches an fp64 sum over exactly-bf16 dyadic operands, and on unit-range inputs lands within an n-squared bar a 0.5 poison leg falls outside
- `test_copy_and_add` - Over tail lengths 1 to 1025, `copy_floats`, `add_inplace` and `add_scale_inplace` land the fp64 result bit for bit on dyadic operands and move every destination element
- `test_mul_scale_axpy` - Over tail lengths 1 to 1025, `mul_inplace`, `scale_inplace` and `axpy` land the fp64 result bit for bit on dyadic operands and move every destination element
- `test_zero_length` - A zero count leaves the destination untouched in every in-place elementwise kernel, and `dot` and `dot_bf16` answer an empty sum of 0
- `test_f32_to_f16_forms` - `cvt_f32_to_f16` bit-matches the float16 cast over the tail sweep, halfway ties, subnormals and signed zeros, and clamps to +-65504 where the cast overflows
- `test_active_q8_repack_layout` - `active_q8_repack_layout` answers the disk-order record (mr 1, kgroup 4, no bias) when not repacked, and the active backend's row tile, k group and weight bias when repacked

### test_matmul_batch.das

`cnt` floats of the file's fill: (i * 7) % 13 scaled by 0.1, less 0.6

- `test_matmul_batch_lanes` - The fp32 `matmul_batch` walk under a job queue lands the one-lane walk's bits exactly at 1152x480 over 300 tokens, where moving one element by 1e-3 shows as a mismatch
- `test_matmul_batch_nest_arm` - The fp32 batch row nest, reached by the knob or through `matmul_batch_rows` at a 128-expert router shape, equals the per-token `matmul` bit for bit, where the shipped tile rounds apart
- `test_matmul_batch` - The fp32 and bf16 batch GEMMs match a double-dot oracle within 1e-5 relative over tile and tail shapes, a poisoned element missing the bar, and the Q8 batch GEMM equals the per-token `matmul_q8q8` exactly
- `test_matmul` - The fp32 `matmul` computes each output as its weight row's dot with x, exactly on small-integer 2x3 and 1x4 cases where every sum is representable
- `test_batch_grid_bit_exact` - On every registered kernel backend the q8q8 batch matmul under the fine and wave-aligned 2-D chunk grids is bit-for-bit the 1-D walk, on starved, ragged-tail and in-cell token-block shapes
- `test_metal_gemm_vs_portable` - The Metal prefill Q8 GEMM donor bit-matches the portable CPU kernel under power-of-two scales on the 32x32 and 64x64 tiles, stays in the f16-tile envelope otherwise, delegates small batches, and leaks nothing

### test_metal_misc_kernels.das

- `test_metal_misc_kernels` - The Metal decode and tower elementwise corpus - argmax and draft top-k, accept and draw, embed gathers, add-rms and norms, activations, im2col, whisper-decoder, hyper-connection mixer and PLE kernels - matches direct CPU oracles on served and tail shapes.
- `test_metal_served` - `metal_served` passes a forward's served or declined answer through unchanged; a served one opens the GPU-served dispatch window, a decline never opens it, and a later decline does not close it.
- `test_metal_region_cat_keys` - `upload_region_cat` keys its cache on every piece: two concats sharing a first piece hold their own second piece's bytes, a repeat returns the cached buffer, and exactly two regions are added.
- `test_metal_ring_slack_reload` - A weights reload drops the mirror ring slack back to `MIRROR_RING_SLACK_MIN` and bumps the arena epoch to stale old encoded steps; a reload already at the floor leaves the epoch where it was.
- `test_metal_mirror_layout_key` - `mirror_layout_key_of` is equal for two shells of one layout and moves when the sliding window, a row prefix, the layer count, the KV ring pin or the ring slack changes, returning when the slack is restored.
- `test_metal_moe_kq_twin_pick` - `metal_moe_kq_twin_pick` gives a crowned family the K-quant MoE twin at every shape, and an uncrowned box the twin only at or under the knee's mean rows per expert, never at a knee of 0.
- `test_lens_tgmem_gate` - A spawned compile of a `metal_dispatch` class with workgroup state and no tgmem= fails naming the gate, while the tgmem= twin, a stamped class and a stamped class with a named kernel all compile.
- `test_lens_max_threads_gate` - A spawned compile refuses `metal_kernel` max_threads = 0 or a string with the positive-int diagnostic, and compiles max_threads = 64 as the control.
- `test_lens_requires_gate` - A spawned compile refuses a `metal_dispatch` requires= item with a non-integer modulus or no percent sign, naming the item grammar, and compiles the well-formed n % 64 twin.
- `test_lens_params_gate` - A spawned compile refuses a `metal_dispatch` params= name no grid=, tg=, requires= or span reads, matching whole identifiers so a substring of another name is still unread, and accepts a requires-only param.
- `test_lens_tgmem_param_gate` - A `metal_dispatch` with workgroup state compiles with no tgmem= when tgmem_param= names a params= entry, and a spawned compile refuses a tgmem_param= naming no param.
- `test_lens_stamp_gate` - A spawned compile refuses a `metal_dispatch` stamp= spec of two tokens, an unknown family, an unserved form, or a class with two kernel methods under one stamp, each with its own diagnostic.
- `test_lens_call_macro_gates` - Spawned compiles refuse `compile_stamp`, `race_pso_pair_stamp`, `race_stems` and `release_handles` at a wrong arity or a source global off the _msl stem, while one named release_handles slot compiles as the control.
- `test_kq_rows_race_verdicts` - The decode race times both arms for every K-quant rows and half-x format in the race table, which covers every served superblock format, with no twin output mismatch, and the crown held after it is the verdict returned.

### test_model_specs.das

- `test_model_specs_invariants` - Every model_specs row has a unique file key and unique display name, every official row pins provenance and parity evidence, and evidence carries exactly one prompt form while arm flags never appear without evidence
- `test_fixture_bar_rule` - `prefix_match_len` stops at the first differing id and at the shorter row's length, and `fixture_ok` holds a whole match under both forms but a partial one only under prefix_bar when it covers at least half the span
- `test_model_spec_views` - `llm_catalog` and `official_catalog` are exact filters of the spec table, `spec_by_file` finds rows by path or base name, `mmproj_companion` pairs vision rows by name, and the image fixture and every companion are pinned on some row
- `test_models_provenance_invariants` - Every `models_provenance` entry is uniquely named under a known root with sha256 or a recipe, fetched entries are https with bytes and sha, and the view holds exactly the pinned text and ASR rows and companions, each once
- `test_quantize_rows` - Every quantize-minted spec row names a fetched source and carries the recipe its quantize spells into the provenance view, `convert_route` picks quantize, canary, no-recipe or a Windows refusal, and `mint_steps` refuses a missing source
- `test_board_provenance` - `board_provenance` holds every official row, the image fixture, every ASR carrier and mmproj and every TTS model, and excludes off-board rows and the tts_oracle parity files
- `test_fetch_models_flags` - fetch_models parses -o NAME into a one-row scope with no board set and --board into the board set with no row scope
- `test_tts_catalog_is_a_view` - `tts_catalog` holds exactly the spec rows carrying a TTS voice, at least five, each found by file through `tts_spec_of`, and an off-board TTS model has no cell

### test_mtp.das

- `test_mtp_loader` - The Qwen3.5-0.8B-MTP GGUF loads 24 trunk layers plus one NextN block with its eh_proj, enorm, hnorm and shared head norm, and with speculation off its trunk continues the plain file's frozen counting fixture token for token
- `test_mtp_output_invariance` - Under pinned kernels, `generate_mtp_greedy` on Qwen3.5-0.8B-MTP emits plain greedy decode's tokens exactly on the accept-heavy counting prompt and the reject-heavier prose prompt, with the head actually drafting
- `test_mtp_depth` - On the CPU rails the k-deep MTP round at depths 2, 3 (forced rejects) and 4 decodes the plain stream token for token, and depth 4 drafts and accepts more than depth 1 over the same 48 tokens, a rerun of depth 1 being the control
- `test_mtp_q4_0` - With the Qwen3.5-0.8B-MTP Q8 file requantized to the q4_0 tier, self-speculative greedy decode emits plain decode's tokens exactly on the counting prompt and the head drafts
- `test_mtp_reject_rollback` - A poisoned 2-row verify undone by `mtp_state_restore`, and a forced-reject round through the engine seam, both leave the next 6 decoded tokens equal to plain decode, and the device counts a rollback exactly when it served the verify
- `test_mtp_prefill_seam` - In a continuation prefill a seam seat that serves leaves the head's poisoned K row untouched after one call for the window's first token and position, a declined seat on a planar model rewrites it on the CPU, and on a blob model nothing writes it
- `test_mtp_verify_window` - A fake prefill driver that serves the CPU MTP round's speculative verify window makes `mtp_spec_eval` panic naming the driver, with the verify-window flag up only while it runs and down for the prompt prefill and after the round
- `test_mtp_invariance_27b` - On Qwen3.6-27B-MTP Q4_K_M, whose draft block sits at layer index 64 where per-layer masks once wrapped, self-speculative greedy decode emits plain decode's counting tokens exactly
- `test_mtp_invariance_glm` - On non-recurrent GLM-4.5-Air with qkv bias and a NextN head, self-speculative decode of a code prompt emits plain decode's tokens exactly, including with every third draft forced through the recr_mask-zero reject branch
- `test_mtp_invariance_flashnext` - Qwen3.8-Flash-Next with its split shared Q8_0 head loads the hyper-connection head mixer, and self-speculative decode of the counting prompt emits plain decode's tokens exactly, forced rejects included

### test_mtp_accept_walks.das

- `test_typical_walk_accepts_the_nucleus` - The typical MTP walk under a 0.9 nucleus accepts a runner-up inside the nucleus and the argmax but not a massless draft at every seed, parks one draw from the cut row's survivors using one random number, and `sample_` returns and clears it
- `test_typical_walk_cuts` - The typical walk rejects exactly the drafts the sampler's cuts remove - the third largest under top-k 2, a token under half the max under min-p 0.5, the third under a 0.6 nucleus over two equal leaders - and parks a survivor
- `test_walk_cuts_at_a_stop` - In both the exact and the typical accept walk a stop-id draft ends the run with the stop as the last accepted token and no parked draw, while without stop ids every matching draft is accepted
- `test_typical_walk_greedy_and_knob` - A penalized greedy sampler's typical walk rejects the repeated draft and parks the penalized argmax with no random draw, and the MtpAccept knob makes a sampled walk accept every in-nucleus runner-up where the exact walk accepts fewer on some seed
- `test_rejection_drafter_records_q` - `mtp_draft_sample` records the sampler's distribution over the head row as q - half each to two equal leaders under a 0.6 nucleus within 1e-5, a point mass for greedy, the two kept under top-k 2 - and draws the draft from it
- `test_rejection_walk_accepts_by_p_over_q` - The rejection walk accepts a draft whose row gives it at least q's mass and rejects one the row gives none at every seed, its residual draw landing on a survivor of the rejecting row and never on the rejected draft
- `test_rejection_walk_top_k_path` - Under top-k 4 the rejection walk accepts a draft at p = q/2 on 160 to 240 of 400 seeds with every reject's residual on the underweighted token, while the p = q control accepts all 400
- `test_rejection_walk_point_mass_q` - With a greedy drafter's point-mass q the rejection walk accepts a draft at p = 1/4 on 70 to 130 of 400 seeds, every reject's residual on the token q gave nothing, while p = 1 accepts all 400
- `test_rejection_walk_accepts_at_half_q_half_the_time` - Under a 0.99 nucleus the rejection walk accepts a draft at p = q/2 on 160 to 240 of 400 seeds with every reject's residual on the token q gave nothing, while the p = q control accepts all 400
- `test_rejection_without_q_records_walks_typical` - Under the rejection knob a round whose drafts recorded no q walks typical, accepting every in-nucleus runner-up, and `mtp_round_begin` clears a previous round's q record so a stale one is never read
- `test_nextn_drafts_sampled_by_mode` - `mtp_drafts_sampled` is false under exact acceptance, true under rejection even at head temperature 0, and false for a greedy stream under rejection
- `test_nextn_draft_temp_records_q` - The NextN head's draft temperature sets q: 0 drafts the argmax as a point mass with no draw, a negative value records the stream's softmax, and 0.5 records the head's softmax at 0.5 within 1e-6 and draws the closed-form cdf pick
- `test_nextn_point_mass_rejection_rate` - At head temperature 0 the rejection walk at p = 1/4 accepts 70 to 130 of 400 seeds with every residual on token 1, while the stream-temperature q control accepts 160 to 240, outside the quarter bound
- `test_dflash_soft_pick_closed_form` - `dflash_soft_pick` records the candidate scores' softmax within 1e-6 at temperatures 1 and 0.5, picks the closed-form cdf draw with one random draw and never the empty slot, and at temperature 0 picks the first best of a tie as a point mass
- `test_dflash_record_q` - `dflash_record_q` records the three non-empty candidates id-ascending, each at its own softmax mass within 1e-7, and a greedy draft as a point mass of one
- `test_dflash_residual_closed_form` - Over 400 seeds the rejection walk of a DFlash draft matches the closed form seed by seed - accept where u times q is under p, else the residual cdf draw off tokens q covers - with the rate within 0.08 of p/q, where a point-mass reading misreads
- `test_verify_scratch_sized_on_a_headless_trunk` - A session over a synthetic trunk with no NextN head still sizes the verify scratch - mtp_cat for MTP_MAX_ROWS rows, the row ids and row 0's logits - while the NextN handoff mtp_h stays empty

### test_mtp_gemma_drafter.das

- `test_gemma_drafter_refusals` - `load_gemma_drafter` refuses a missing path and a magic-less file with a reason and no weights, and the sidecar resolver finds the gemma4-assistant head beside UD, K-quant and i-quant trunks but never a qwen35 NextN head of the same name
- `test_gemma_drafter_attach_checks` - The drafter attach's target check names a short trunk or a capture layer's mismatched head size or kv heads, the facade joins every backend's refusal, and the Vulkan driver check names the first missing fact while a complete driver passes
- `test_gemma_drafter_bind_ladder` - `assist_bind_rung` stops at the first failing rung - no armed driver, another codec, past the region's context, no free region - binds otherwise, and binds a session that owns its region whatever the others hold
- `test_gemma_drafter_gather_refusal` - The Metal drafter attach refuses a metal-blob trunk shell of the drafter's geometry whose token table the device gathers no row of, naming the table, and the shell cannot speculate
- `test_gemma_drafter_q40_head` - Loading the Q4_0 gemma-4 drafter head fails with a reason naming the tensor's Q4_0 type and the expected Q8_0
- `test_gemma_drafter_load` - The gemma-4-26B Q8_0 drafter sidecar loads with the contract's dims, per-layer head sizes, kv heads, sliding flags, capture layers 28,28,28,29 and layer scales, its blob the exact padded Q8_0 byte sum with every tensor 32-byte aligned
- `test_gemma_drafter_ple_refusal` - The drafter attach refuses the gemma-4 E2B trunk naming its per-layer embeddings and the E2B cannot speculate, while the same config without per-layer embeddings refuses on another clause
- `test_gemma_drafter_cpu_step` - One CPU reference drafter step on gemma-4-26B, seeded with the target's argmax and its live K/V and hidden, yields finite vocab-wide logits, an in-range draft token and a finite nonzero h_next
- `test_gemma_drafter_gpu_step` - The GPU drafter step on the served 26B agrees with the CPU oracle's draft token and sits within the home's logits and h_next bars (0.25 and 0.05 on Metal, 1.0 on a Q8_0 feed) at a short anchor and past the sliding window, an off-by-one seed landing outside
- `test_gemma_drafter_served` - A scheduler speculating at depth 1 through the attached gemma-4 drafter emits the plain scheduler's counting tokens exactly, every draft counted by the device drafter, and with the drafter detached it stands down, drafts nothing, and still matches
- `test_gemma_drafter_verify_decline` - On Metal a joint drafter verify over two streams on two KV codecs carries no stream and counts no round, each stream's step equal bit for bit to a plain decode step, while one codec across both carries both streams
- `test_gemma_drafter_depth_knob` - At drafter depths 3 and 1 the speculating scheduler drafts k tokens a round and emits the plain scheduler's counting tokens exactly across a page boundary, and a reasoning budget lands its forced close at the budget with the plain stream's tokens
- `test_gemma_drafter_joint` - Three speculating streams at depths 1 and 2 ride one joint verify a tick, each emitting the plain scheduler's counting tokens exactly, while a lone stream counts no joint verify (the counter's control)
- `test_gemma_drafter_codecs` - On q8_0 and tq4 KV mirrors the drafter's rounds run on the device, accept drafts, and the speculating scheduler emits the same codec's plain scheduler tokens exactly
- `test_gemma_drafter_past_ring` - Past a sliding capture layer's KV ring the drafter at the same anchor drafts the flat mirror's tokens - logits bit for bit off Metal, the same pick on Metal - and the ringed stream matches the flat one with acceptance within 10 percent
- `test_gemma_drafter_kquant_table` - The drafter attaches to the UD-IQ3_XXS 26B trunk whose Q6_K token table the seed embed gathers, accepts drafts at depth 2, and emits the plain scheduler's counting tokens exactly

### test_mtp_sampled_walk.das

- `test_landed_sampler_matches_the_row_sampler` - The landed sampler drawing off an oracle-built selection landing picks the row sampler's token under nucleus, top-k, min-p and penalties, lands rows late on its refusals, and its MTP walks, q cap and chain-cut probability match the rows
- `test_sampled_walk_matches_plain_sampled_decode` - When every draft is its row's only token with mass, the sampled MTP walk accepts all three and parks plain sampled decode's fourth draw from the same seed, with one RNG draw per emitted token and `sample_` returning and clearing the parked token
- `test_sampled_walk_stops_at_the_first_miss` - The sampled walk stops at the first draft its row gives no mass, accepting one draft and parking plain sampled decode's second draw, never the rejected draft, with the RNG state matching after two draws
- `test_greedy_walk_with_penalties_goes_through_the_sampler` - A bare argmax sampler keeps the argmax walk, while a penalized temperature-0 sampler routes through the sampled walk, rejecting the repeated draft and parking the penalized argmax with no random draw
- `test_sampled_walk_penalizes_with_the_accepted_drafts` - Under top-k 1 with a repetition penalty the sampled walk counts each accepted draft into the recent window, so a draft repeating the first is rejected and the runner-up parked, and the window is put back afterwards
- `test_sampled_flag_stands_the_greedy_chain_down` - `sample_` clears the session's sampled flag under a bare argmax sampler and sets it under a temperature or a temperature-0 penalty, the cases whose pick can differ from the raw argmax

### test_mtp_snapshot.das

- `test_first_snapshot_of_a_large_recurrent_state` - A first `mtp_state_snapshot` of a 151 MB deltanet state past the unreserved-growth guard holds every float, and `mtp_state_restore` puts back every lane span, the conv state, the position, the n-gram window and the PLE ring row
- `test_per_position_accept_telemetry` - `mtp_pos_report` prints each drafted depth's hits over tries since the reset (2/3, 1/2, 0/1 for three noted rounds), omits a depth never drafted, and is empty after `mtp_pos_reset`
- `test_mtp_round_cold_why` - `mtp_round_cold_why` returns empty for a warm round and names each single failing arm - position 0, a hidden row carried for another position, a row narrower than the drafter, a depth running past the context - with the host predicate agreeing
- `test_dn_capture_contract` - `dn_capture_begin` opens one unfilled state-sized snapshot per ascending stop inside the window and panics by name on a model with no recurrent state or a stop outside the window or out of order, and `dn_capture_check` refuses unfilled captures

### test_mxfp4.das

- `test_e8m0_half` - `e8m0_half` decodes E8M0 scale bytes to exact powers of two - 127 to 0.5, 128 to 1.0 - including the denormal bit patterns at 0 and 1, FLT_MIN at 2 and 2^126 at 254
- `test_dot_mx4q8` - The scalar MXFP4 x Q8 dot matches an fp64 elementwise dequant reference within 1e-5 relative, and the TBL+SDOT dot matches the scalar leaf within 1e-6 at n 96, 128 and 256, the 96 covering the unroll tail
- `test_matmul_mx4q8` - `matmul_mx4q8` matches the per-row scalar leaf within 1e-6 relative on 5 rows under the active backend and every row-major backend, and on arm64-gen after `repack_mx4_weight` on 6 rows including the 2 tail rows

### test_nmt.das

The exact lane's stage bar: max |got - want| over the stage's largest magnitude, the decoder's stages under the oracle's own tokens (reads 4e-6 to 6e-6 on the M5 Max, `run.das -- --area translate`, -jit, the m5 profile).

- `test_nmt_spm` - The SentencePiece model-file tokenizer encodes every Bergamot fixture line and normalizer edge line to Python sentencepiece's ids exactly, while dropping the charsmap misspells some edge line (the control)
- `test_nmt_exact_lane` - Under marian's forced tokens the Bergamot exact lane matches the f32 oracle's dump at every stage within 1e-4 of the stage's max magnitude, and its free run agrees on at least 28 lines, with displaced-token and displaced-source controls outside
- `test_nmt_q8_lane` - The ru/en Bergamot q8 lane serves its GEMMs and classifier off the Q8_0 plane and translates at least 25 fixture lines as the f32 oracle does, while zeroing the Q8_0 classifier moves every line and falls under the floor
- `test_nmt_device` - The device translation seat serves every ru/en fixture line, at least 26 matching the CPU q8 chain, across a model swap with no shutdown; a zeroed device classifier changes every line, and shape, length, buffer and quant_mode declines translate on the CPU
- `test_nmt_float32_student` - A synthetic float32 Marian student stages to f32 planes bit-identical to its intgemm8 twin's with every [in][out] GEMM transposed, an untransposed twin differing (the control), and the q8 lane lays the classifier's Q8_0 copy after the GEMMs
- `test_nmt_loader_refusals` - `stage_nmt_model` stages a well-formed synthetic student and refuses by name each malformed one - wrong yml values, missing or misshaped items, bad framing, a split or BPE or absent vocabulary, a missing model
- `test_nmt_spm_file_refusals` - `load_spm_model_file` reads a trainer spec carrying a fixed64 field with every piece and later field intact, and refuses by name a varint cut at the end, a group wire type, and a field running past its message
- `test_translate_facade_contracts` - The translator facade refuses an LLM with no direction or a self-direction, serves any two of its 46 languages, holds a Marian student to its own pair, and loads a synthetic student on the q8 lane by default and f32 under exact
- `test_nmt_llm_translator` - MiLMMT-46 through the facade translates ru to en (pharmacy) and back, stopping at the end of the first line where an unstopped completion runs on, its baked .dlim translates too, and a Bergamot student keeps its one direction
- `test_nmt_chat_translator` - Qwen3-4B-Instruct through the translator facade's chat template translates a Russian sentence to one English line naming the pharmacy, with no reasoning block
- `test_nmt_chat_thinking_off` - Hybrid-thinking Qwen3.5-0.8B through the translator facade answers with thinking off: a translation naming the pharmacy, no think block, within a 48-token reply
- `test_nmt_step_lanes_and_device_gate` - `nmt_step_lanes` gives a 512/2048 student up to eight lanes and a tiny step one, follows the lane-work seam and its restore, and `nmt_device_shape_ok` serves the students' geometry but declines widths off the 64-wide tiles and bad head splits

### test_par_indexed.das

- `test_maybe_parallel_for_bool_no_que` - With no job queue, the bool form of `maybe_parallel_for` with a true flag runs one inline invoke over the whole range and bumps the inline counter by exactly one
- `test_single_thread` - Single-thread mode makes every dispatch form run inline with exactly-once coverage on team and fifo queues, turning it off restores dispatch, and hybrid phase parking leaves the worker limit alone under it
- `test_single_thread_env` - A child process started with DASLLAMA_SINGLE_THREAD=1 reads the flag at context init, dispatches none of three rounds and prints the announce once; unset, it dispatches all three and stays silent
- `test_maybe_parallel_for_indexed` - `maybe_parallel_for_indexed` covers every index exactly once with slots inside the dispatch bound and per-slot checksums summing exactly, inline, in team and fifo modes, and under a worker limit

### test_parity.das

- `test_parity_tied_cls_q8_rows` - A tied Q8 load of SmolLM2-135M takes the cls_q8 path, and its dequantized embedding rows for four tokens are bit-identical to the fp32 table an fp32 load decodes
- `test_parity_untied_emb_q8_rows` - An untied Q8 load of stories15M drops the fp32 embedding table for the emb_q8 plane, whose rows and `embed_row` output are bit-identical to the fp32 load's table
- `test_parity_specs` - Every model_specs row with a pinned parity fixture generates its frozen greedy ids token for token (or to the half-span prefix bar, with a flipped-id control), including its chunked, reference and per-expert prefill arms
- `test_parity_gptoss_20b` - gpt-oss-20b on one Q8 load reproduces its frozen greedy ids token for token on the short spec fixture and on a 449-token counting prompt that engages the 128-token sliding window
- `test_parity_dump_refuses_foreign_files` - `parity_dump_refusal` names a foreign magic word, a different version word and a missing file as refusals, and accepts a header carrying this build's magic and version
- `test_parity_dump_round_trip` - On Qwen3.5-0.8B-MTP the device-arm dump reads back bit-exact, the CPU arm replayed on its prompt, feed and tape matches every row within the 0.20 relative bar, a one-row poison reds only that row, and a changed feed is refused

### test_parity_pregate.das

- `test_parity_pregate_ids_form` - The board pregate `parity_check` passes Qwen3-0.6B's pinned-ids fixture, fails it with the last id flipped, and refuses a spec with no evidence
- `test_fixture_gate` - The timed run's `fixture_gate_check` passes the table's fixture on a loaded Qwen3-0.6B, refuses an opening with every id shifted, and passes a row with no evidence
- `test_parity_pregate_prefix_bar` - With prefix_bar set, a Llama-3.2-1B fixture whose tail half is flipped still passes `parity_check` while a flip inside the first half fails, and the strict form fails the same flipped tail
- `test_parity_pregate_text_form` - The gemma-4-E2B text-form fixture, encoded through the model's tokenizer, reproduces its pinned continuation under `parity_check`
- `test_parity_pregate_kq_native` - The Qwen3-4B Q4_K_M row's kq-native load reproduces its pinned continuation under `parity_check`, and the pregate restores the kquant-native mode it flipped
- `test_parity_last_layer_slice` - On the resident Vulkan driver, a 512-token Llama-3.2-1B prefill with the last layer's FFN sliced yields logits bit-identical to the whole-window prefill, split-k pinned off for both arms

### test_parrot.das

- `test_vad_resampler` - Parrot's 24 to 16 kHz VAD resampler yields 16000 linearly interpolated samples per second, a stream fed in drains of any size is sample-identical to one fed at once, and `vad_to_mic` maps indices back by 3/2
- `test_take_rules` - A take ends exactly at two seconds of post-speech quiet, at the cap, or after six silent device seconds, and `clip_window` pads speech by a quarter second clamped to the take and never longer than the cap
- `test_panels` - Parrot's panels: the silence countdown shows seconds left only after speech and never below zero, waveform min/max columns grown in drains equal those built at once, and a say reads out only when every chunk played
- `test_smoke_clones_and_says` - The parrot example's smoke run clones a voice from the JFK clip, says the text in it with over two seconds of speech played at least 80 percent through, and a non-audio --clip is refused by name

### test_plane.das

- `test_plane_float_binds_and_reads` - A PlaneF bound to a 128-byte section reports 32 elements, is not empty, and reads the exact floats written there through both int and int64 indices
- `test_plane_float_offset_section` - A PlaneF bound at byte offset 64 has 16 elements and its element 0 is element 16 of the whole run, so reads start at the bind offset rather than the base
- `test_plane_float_rejects_ragged_section` - Binding a PlaneF to 126 bytes, not a whole number of floats, is declined and leaves the plane empty with length 0 instead of rounding
- `test_plane_int8_binds_and_reads` - A PlaneI8 over a 16-byte section counts one element per byte and reads the values back signed, -8 through 7
- `test_plane_at_refuses_past_the_end` - `plane_at` one element past the end of a float plane and of a byte plane panics with text naming the offset and the plane's range, while the end offset itself does not panic
- `test_plane_at_is_the_hot_path_form` - `plane_at` returns a raw pointer at an element offset whose reads match the backing floats, and the end offset yields a non-null pointer
- `test_plane_release_owns_nothing` - `plane_release` leaves the plane empty with a null pointer and the backing bytes intact, so a fresh plane rebinds and reads the same values
- `test_plane_two_views_one_backing` - Two overlapping PlaneF views of one backing both bind, and the same byte reads the same value through either view

### test_ple_check.das

- `test_ple_check_table` - The `ple_check_table` go-live tripwire panics on an empty or one-byte-short PLE table plane for every format arm (q8, k4/k5/k6/q40, q51/q5032), passes when the table is resident, and exempts a non-PLE model
